settings.standfirst: Everything owners ask us before they buy: sizing, foam, washing, delivery and returns.

settings.heading: The questions we get asked most.

settings.question: How do I know which size to get?
settings.answer:
Measure your dog from nose to base of tail while they're lying stretched out, then add 15–20cm. If they fall between two sizes, go up: dogs that sprawl need the length more than you'd think.

Still unsure? The Bed Finder asks four quick questions about how your dog sleeps and suggests one bed in the right size.

settings.question: Which kind of bed suits the way my dog sleeps?
settings.answer: Curlers usually love a nest or donut bed with raised sides to tuck into. Dogs who lean against things want a bolster to rest their head on. Sprawlers need a flat mattress with room to stretch out. Older dogs, and dogs who are slower getting up, do best on a supportive memory-foam core.

settings.question: What does 50kg/m³ actually mean?
settings.answer:
It's how much foam is packed into every cubic metre. Density isn't the same as firmness: a low-density foam can feel firm on day one and still collapse by month six. High-density foam keeps its structure under repeated weight, which is why a 50kg/m³ core is still supporting hips and elbows years later.

You'll find this core in the orthopaedic beds. The fibre-filled nest beds are built for softness instead, and each product page says which is which.

settings.question: Will it help a dog with arthritis or hip problems?
settings.answer: These beds spread your dog's weight so pressure isn't concentrated on hips, elbows and shoulders, which is what makes lying down and getting back up harder for a dog with joint wear. A bed isn't a treatment and won't replace veterinary care, so please keep talking to your vet. What it can change is the surface they spend fourteen hours a day on.

settings.question: Can I actually wash it?
settings.answer:
On most of the range, yes: properly, not just a spot-clean. Covers zip off and go straight in the machine at 30°C, and on the orthopaedic beds a waterproof inner liner keeps wet coats, muddy paws and accidents away from the foam.

One exception worth knowing before you buy: waterproof-fabric beds are wiped clean rather than washed with detergent, because detergent strips the coating. Every product page says which applies.
